items.title: Community Delegation - Mr. Robert Musselman re Proposal re
notes: Biological Fertilizer

Sloping Acres Inc. owns several farms in Centre Wellington and a related business. They are requesting to bore a pipe under 8th line and Middlebrook Road for the purpose of pumping fertilizer. A map was provided of the road route travelled to spread fertilizer currently. He further outlined what he believes the benefits to the Township are to permitting the pipeline.

notes: meeting.
2024 Downtown Parking Strategy
Report from D. Wilson, Chief Administrative Officer
Dan Wilson, Chief Administrative Officer introduced the Municipal Parking Strategy and the consultant Gordon Hui from RJ Burnside & Associates Limited.

Gordon Hui outlined the phases of the parking study including a review of the study process and the parking needs and opportunities, as well as presented the draft recommendations and financial considerations.

The recommendations, as a result of the study, include increasing the parking supply with joint use agreements with private spaces, utilizing the parking lot at the Jefferson Elora Community Centre, planning for the construction of a parking garage/structure and consideration of paid parking implementation options. In addition, active transportation can lessen the parking burden through bike shares and a shuttle bus program.

Mr. Hui further outlined the financial considerations including the estimated expense for a parking structure, joint use agreements, shuttle bus, enforcement, and paid parking implementation. He further outlined the anticipated revenue generation from paid parking and enforcement.
D. Wilson outlined the staff recommendation including the requests for 2024. He indicated anything beyond 2024 will come forward in a future Council report.
Councillor Lustgarten-Evoy requested meetings be set with the BIA’s to review the options.

Staff responded to questions regarding the enforcement of 3 hour parking, shuttle stops and parking for the shuttle stops, accessible parking for churches and medical offices, how growth was included in the determination of the parking needs, and the cost to expand the program outside of the downtown areas.
Further discussion occurred around the topics of parking enforcement, paid parking and issuing parking passes.
Council recessed from 8:05pm to 8:12pm

items.title: Municipal Class Environmental Assessment Study: Preliminary
notes: Preferred Alternative for Bridges 1-P, 28-P, 30-P, 32-P, and 33-P Report from A. Dickieson, Engineering Services Coordinator Adam Dickieson, Engineering Services Coordinator gave a presentation indicating the Municipal Class Environmental Assessment Study recommends the preferred option for each bridge within the study. He reviewed the process including public consultation, feedback received, alternative solutions considered, evaluation criteria, and the preferred alternative to reopen 28-P, 32-P and 33-P and removal of bridge 1-P and 30-P. He further reviewed the bridge replacement timeline which includes construction in 2027.
